text:
marco: Heads-up — I sketched a surgical plan to prune the core shared-state surface without a full rewrite. Want quick sync before we spin up the spike.
sarah: love the framing. can you paste the high-level steps?
marco: Sure — 1) introduce a thin accessor Facade around the shared state, 2) add a namespaced staging area per-tenant, 3) migrate hot paths incrementally behind feature flags, 4) remove legacy writes once telemetry shows 99.99% reads routed to new accessor.
alex: sounds good. question: how do we handle concurrent readers/writers during migration? that's where most risk is.
marco: plan is optimistic: keep current locking semantics, add a write-forwarding shim that duplicates writes to new namespaced store and marks them as 'migrated'. reads prefer the new store when key present. fallback to old store on misses.
jasmin: duplication means we pay double for writes during migration window — rough estimate?
marco: ballpark for typical traffic: +5–7% GPU host I/O and ~3% increased S3 ops for 2–3 weeks. will add a throttling policy if it spikes.
devops-bot: @channel Canary job scheduled: state-prune-canary on staging at 11:30am PT.
sarah: great — what are our SLO/rollback criteria for canary?
marco: Canary success = 0 user-facing errors, <0.1% read fallback rate, write duplication latency increase <20ms p50. Rollback triggers: any increase in 5xx rate or fallback >1% sustained for 15m.
kyle: we should also add an invariant check in the accessor: for any migrated key read from new store must equal old store value for first 24h. fail-fast metric to alert on divergence.
jasmin: agree. can we do a streaming diff for large blobs?
marco: yes — we'll checksum prefixes and only stream full objects when checksums mismatch. saves bandwidth.
sarah: testing notes: unit + integration + property tests around concurrent writes, and a chaos test to drop duplicate writes mid-flight. Also add long tail latency probe.
alex: owner for telemetry dashboard? need token-level breakdown, per-route fallback, and migration progress by tenant.
marco: assigning to alex for dashboard + jasmin for cost guardrails. I'll do the accessor + shim PR.
devops-bot: @marco PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4591 — merge queueing.
jasmin: before merge, include a short migration runbook with steps to throttle or disable new write-forwarding. Ops should be able to flip a kill-switch without deploy.
marco: will add a runtime flag behind "state.prune.enable", and an emergency route that flips to passthrough mode.
kyle: retention / GC concerns: once we stop legacy writes, we need a safe TTL for the old namespace and a cleanup job. recommend 30 days default, configurable per-tenant.
sarah: legal/regulatory note: some tenants may require longer retention. add per-tenant override and include compliance approval step in rollout checklist.
alex: timeline?
marco: spike this week -> canary on staging Wednesday -> limited prod canary next Monday (10% traffic, opt-in tenants) -> full rollout 3 weeks after if metrics stable.
jasmin: logging: tag every duplicated write with migration_id and include sampling for full payloads.
marco: agreed. also adding a regression alert if model quality (eval set) degrades after migration for any route.
kyle: oncall: please notify eng-oncall and eng-runtime before prod canary, and attach rollback runbook to the alert.
sarah: I'll draft the RFC addendum summarizing tradeoffs (cost, complexity, rollback surface, compliance) and link PRs.
marco: thanks — if nobody objects I’ll merge the spike branch Friday morning and start tests. objection window 24h. :thumbsup:
